artifacts.notes: One page image, leaf n254: cols. 501-502, 1889 by 3059 pixels. Read on this image, across the foot of both columns after Homilia CVII: 'HOMILIA CVIII. Super illa Evangelii Matth. cap. IX: Ascendit Jesus in naviculam, et transfretavit. ADMONITIO. In Breviario Romano pars hujus homiliae legitur in dominica 18 post Pentecosten sub nomine S. Petri Chrysologi, quam eidem clarissimus vir Sebastianus Pauli Cler. Reg. a Matre Dei in sua ejusdem S. Ravennatensis archiepiscopi editione Venet. an. 1750 ascripsit, quemadmodum multo ante Combefisius tom. VII, pag. 397, aliique. Haec esse tanti momenti mihi videntur, ut communiter receptam non audeam impugnare sententiam; licere tamen mihi arbitror veterum referre scriptorum opinionem. In bibliotheca enim Vaticana codicem invenimus num. 6451, qui, pag. 19, S. Joannem Osaureum, sive Chrysostomum homiliae auctorem appellat; in archivo Casinensi codex 102, pag. 253, eam S. Severiano episcopo tribuit. At duos alios codices non infimae notae in S. Maximum Taurinensem convenire attestamur, nempe Vaticanum 4222 pag. 341, et Laurentianum 36 Plut. XVII pag. 251, expresse enim post Evangelii locum habent: Homilia S. Maximi episcopi. Hujusmodi testimonia a styli similitudine confirmari possunt. Verum etsi forte nostra nos fallat opinio, rem tamen gratam aequis lectoribus nos fecisse existimamus, cum huic homiliae variantes plurimas ex codice Vaticano 6451 collectas subjiciamus.' The printing divides 'Osaureum' as 'Osavreum'. The homily's text begins in col. 502 'Christum in humanis actibus divina gessisse my-'. One leaf only.

passages.context: Homilia CVIII, 'Super illa Evangelii Matth. cap. IX: Ascendit Jesus in naviculam, et transfretavit', with Bruni's admonition on its ascription and a short argument: the text Patrologia Latina 52 prints as Peter Chrysologus's Sermo 50, De paralytico curato, on Matthew 9:1-8.
passages.notes: LOCUS, read on page images: PL 57:501-506, heading and admonition at the foot of cols. 501-502 (leaf n254), text to col. 506, where Homilia CIX follows. The line range includes notes on Homilia CVII printed at the foot of those columns. The wording of this OCR layer is not collated as a whole; what these records quote was read on leaves n254 and n255. The admonition, quoted in full on leaf n254's artifact record, reports that part of the homily is read in the Roman Breviary on the Eighteenth Sunday after Pentecost under Peter Chrysologus's name; that Sebastiano Pauli's Venice edition of 1750 ascribed it to him, as Combefis had long before; that Vatican codex 6451 names John Chrysostom as its author, Monte Cassino codex 102 Severian, and Vatican 4222 and Laurentianus 36 Plut. XVII, 'non infimae notae', Maximus. Bruni declines to impugn the commonly received ascription, reports the older one, says style could confirm it, allows that his opinion may be wrong, and prints the homily among Maximus's Homiliae de diversis, not in the volume's appendix of doubtful works (cols. 849-956). Neither the Breviary lesson nor any of the manuscripts is held or checked here; these are the admonition's statements. Where this edition and Patrologia Latina 52 differ in wording, and on the 'non respicit' reading they share, see passage.peter-chrysologus.sermones.1894-garnier-migne-pl-52.sermo-50.

work.author: Maximus of Turin, bishop of Turin, as Bruno Bruni's edition ascribes them
work.description: The hundred and eighteen homilies that Bruno Bruni's edition of Maximus of Turin, made at the command of Pius VI, distributes into four classes -- hiemales de tempore, aestivae de tempore, de sanctis and de diversis -- as Migne's Patrologia Latina 57 reprints them; its Elenchus lists them from col. 221. A locus is Bruni's homily number. Homilia CVIII, on Matthew 9:1 'Ascendit Jesus in naviculam', is the text Patrologia Latina 52 prints as Peter Chrysologus's Sermo 50, and its admonition records the conflicting ascriptions.
work.title: Homiliae
